sourceScope: Amari Explore & Languages only; Askia is storage-isolation coverage, not a normal-route game player

questions.prompt: Find Antarctica on the map.
questions.fact: Antarctica is the cold continent at the bottom of the map. It has no countries.

questions.prompt: Find Australia on the map.
questions.fact: Australia is the continent. Oceania is a wider region that includes Australia, New Zealand and Pacific islands.

questions.prompt: Find North America on the map.
questions.fact: Canada and Mexico are in North America.

questions.prompt: Which map key would help a sailor find the harbour?
questions.fact: A map key explains symbols. An anchor can show a harbour.

questions.prompt: Find South America on the map.
questions.fact: Brazil and Peru are in South America.

questions.prompt: Which ocean circles Antarctica?
questions.fact: The Southern Ocean circles Antarctica.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of England?
questions.fact: London is the capital city of England and of the United Kingdom.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Wales?
questions.fact: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is around the North Pole?
questions.fact: The Arctic Ocean is around the North Pole.

questions.prompt: Which way is east on our map?
questions.fact: With north at the top, east is to the right.

questions.prompt: Australia is on which continent?
questions.fact: Australia is the continent. Oceania is a wider region around it.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a careful comparison?
questions.fact: Some tropical places are often warm, but weather can change. We should not say every island is the same.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is around the North Pole?
questions.fact: The Arctic Ocean is around the North Pole.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is the biggest?
questions.fact: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is between the Americas and Europe/Africa?
questions.fact: The Atlantic Ocean sits between these continents.

questions.prompt: A time detective wants to learn what an old seaside holiday looked like. Which clue is most useful?
questions.fact: An old photograph can show visible details, but it cannot tell us everything people thought or felt.

questions.prompt: Put these lights from oldest to newest.
questions.fact: People used fire before candles, and electric lightbulbs came later.

questions.prompt: A photograph of an old house can show us what?
questions.fact: A photograph is useful evidence for what a place looked like, but it cannot show every thought.

questions.prompt: Which source could help us investigate a castle long ago?
questions.fact: An artefact is one object from the past. Historians compare it with other sources.

questions.prompt: Put these ways to send a message from oldest to newest.
questions.fact: A handwritten letter is older than a landline telephone, which is older than a smartphone message.

questions.prompt: A photograph of an old house can show us what?
questions.fact: A photograph is useful evidence for what a place looked like, but it cannot show every thought.

questions.prompt: Put these school photographs in time order using their dates.
questions.fact: Dates help us order sources. 1990 came before 2010, and 2010 came before 2025.

questions.prompt: Which clues could help us find out how a local school changed?
questions.fact: Photographs and an interview give different clues. Memories and pictures can both leave things out.

questions.prompt: Put these lights from oldest to newest.
questions.fact: People used fire before candles, and electric lightbulbs came later.

questions.prompt: Put these parts of a person’s story from earliest to latest.
questions.fact: A personal timeline starts with being a baby, then a child, then an adult. People grow at different rates.

questions.prompt: Put these lights from oldest to newest.
questions.fact: People used fire before candles, and electric lightbulbs came later.

questions.prompt: Put these ways to send a message from oldest to newest.
questions.fact: A handwritten letter is older than a landline telephone, which is older than a smartphone message.

questions.prompt: A photograph of an old house can show us what?
questions.fact: A photograph is useful evidence for what a place looked like, but it cannot show every thought.

questions.prompt: Which source could help us investigate a castle long ago?
questions.fact: An artefact is one object from the past. Historians compare it with other sources.

questions.prompt: Which pair gives two different kinds of clues about how a local street changed?
questions.fact: An old photo can show what the street looked like, while a modern map can show today’s layout. Comparing them helps us notice change.

questions.prompt: Which one is an animal?
questions.fact: A frog is an animal. Animals move, feed and grow.

questions.prompt: A window must be see-through. Which material is useful?
questions.fact: Clear glass is transparent, so we can see through it. The window is the object; glass is its material.

questions.prompt: Which one is a plant?
questions.fact: An oak tree is a plant. It grows and needs light and water.

questions.prompt: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.fact: A rabbit is a mammal. Trout are fish and frogs are amphibians.

questions.prompt: Which season often has the warmest days?
questions.fact: Summer often has the warmest days, although weather can change.

questions.prompt: Which part helps hold a plant upright and carries water upwards?
questions.fact: The stem helps support the plant and carries water to other parts.

questions.prompt: Which tool can help us observe a small leaf closely?
questions.fact: A hand lens magnifies small details so we can observe closely.

questions.prompt: Which season often has the warmest days?
questions.fact: Summer often has the warmest days, although weather can change.

questions.prompt: What does a green plant need to grow?
questions.fact: Plants need water and light to grow.

questions.prompt: Which change might we observe as spring begins?
questions.fact: Plants may grow new leaves or flowers in spring. Weather varies, so this is an observation to check, not a promise for every day.

questions.prompt: Predict: two similar seedlings get the same light and warmth. Only one gets water. What might happen?
questions.fact: Your prediction came first. Then you compared it with the observation. This test gives evidence that growing seedlings need water.

questions.prompt: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.fact: A rabbit is a mammal. Trout are fish and frogs are amphibians.

questions.prompt: In “a wooden chair”, which word names the material?
questions.fact: A chair is an object. Wood is the material it can be made from.

questions.prompt: Which season often has the warmest days?
questions.fact: Summer often has the warmest days, although weather can change.

questions.prompt: Which animal is a bird?
questions.fact: A robin is a bird. A lizard is a reptile and a cat is a mammal.

questions.prompt: Which is a physical feature of a place?
questions.fact: A beach is a natural physical feature. A school and road are human-made features.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is the biggest?
questions.fact: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean.

questions.prompt: Find Asia on the map.
questions.fact: Asia is the largest continent. Japan and India are in Asia.

questions.prompt: Find South America on the map.
questions.fact: Brazil and Peru are in South America.

questions.prompt: Find Europe on the map.
questions.fact: Europe is north of Africa. The United Kingdom and France are in Europe.

questions.prompt: Guide the boat to the treasure using compass directions.
questions.fact: You followed north, east, north, east. A compass and map help us describe a route.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
questions.fact: The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland.

questions.prompt: Brazil is in which continent?
questions.fact: Brazil is a country in South America.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shaped more like the round Earth?
questions.fact: A globe is a round model of Earth. A flat map spreads places onto a page or screen.

questions.prompt: Which way is east on our map?
questions.fact: With north at the top, east is to the right.
